findings.title: VOBIZ_CALLER_ID still present in the production env after the Vobiz removal
findings.evidence: ssh ... grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' /opt/leadgen/.env shows VOBIZ_CALLER_ID; grep shows live readers in app/telephony/compliance.py:238, app/telephony/telephony_service.py:374, app/telephony/telephony_readiness_probe.py:63. FIXED 2026-09-19: ComplianceGate._caller_id() read ONLY settings.vobiz_caller_id / VOBIZ_CALLER_ID, so removing VOBIZ_* (the mandated cleanup) would have blocked 100% of promotional calls as no_caller_id. Red/green proof: with only TATA_SMARTFLO_DID set, pre-fix _caller_id() returned '' (AssertionError: assert '' == '+911140000001'); post-fix it returns the DID. tests/test_compliance.py 4 new tests + 95-test telephony suite green.
findings.blast_radius: Was: a removed provider's caller-id variable was a hard dependency of the dial path (latent silent revenue stop) and misconfigured caller-id trips a compliance reason.
findings.next_step: DONE in code. Remaining owner step: remove VOBIZ_* from the prod env + app/config.py:vobiz_caller_id -- calls no longer depend on it, and the legacy read now logs a one-time warning so the removal is observable.

findings.title: Admin-created users never received their verification email
findings.evidence: app/api/admin.py imported EmailSender from app.platform.auto_outreach (name does not exist there) inside a try/except that logged at DEBUG; the API was also wrong (send() vs await send_email(to_emails=...)).
findings.blast_radius: Every admin-created account silently skipped onboarding email; failure was invisible in logs.
findings.next_step: Fixed: canonical import + async API + WARNING-level failure logging + regression guard tests/test_admin_verification_email.py.

findings.title: agent_talent_pool makes 992 TypeSafe API calls and discards the judgment
findings.evidence: app/platform/agent_talent_pool.py: 31 agents x 32 specializations = 992 sequential typesafe_choice() HTTP calls at build time; the returned specialization is looked up in a hardcoded snake_case capability map, so a human-readable answer ('Cold call expert') falls through to 'general'. Repo-wide grep: zero code consumers.
findings.blast_radius: No runtime caller today, so no live outage — but any future call to get_talent_pool() blocks for ~30 minutes of paid API calls, and the file was the app's ONLY TypeSafe consumer, so the decision layer looked integrated while being decorative. Conflicts with the canonical 31-agent registry (ADR-164/165).
findings.next_step: Fixed: orphan removed (rollback: git checkout d4243e7a -- app/platform/agent_talent_pool.py); tests/test_typesafe_consumer_inventory.py now allowlist TypeSafe consumers so a decorative one cannot return silently.

findings.title: TypeSafe is effectively unused across the product
findings.evidence: grep app/ for typesafe_integration|get_typesafe_client|typesafe_choice|typesafe_noul|typesafe_score -> no product module consumes a TypeSafe judgment; app/platform/automation_health.py reads credential_state() only (config check, no judgment).
findings.blast_radius: Every semantic decision the owner wants TypeSafe to own (lead qualification, next-action, risk triage) is still made by ad-hoc heuristics or not at all. The integration is INERT even with a valid key.
findings.next_step: Wire one real consumer end-to-end with a trace record and a consumed downstream action (admin triage script is the first; a revenue-path consumer is still missing).

findings.title: TypeSafe key exposed in git history must be rotated
findings.evidence: Commit 7317f990 hardcoded a live ~100-char key as the os.getenv fallback default; 979c2229 removed the literal but the value remains in history. Live probe of the historical fingerprint fe66d7de1807 -> HTTP 401 (no longer valid).
findings.blast_radius: History exposure only. Residual risk is low because the exposed key is already rejected, but rotation is still the correct close-out.
findings.next_step: Owner rotates at platform.typesafe.ai (or explicitly accepts the already-401 stale exposure).

findings.title: Local orchestrator ledger was JSON-clobbered into a SQLite path
findings.evidence: data/orchestrator_ledger.db first bytes were 7B 0D 0A 20 20 22 64 65 76 5F 77 6F 72 6B 65 72 (JSON) though the durable task store opens it as SQLite. DevWorkerProver now writes data/dev_workers_ledger.json. Local file already absent. FIXED 2026-09-19: root cause was DurableTaskStore._init_sqlite() running CREATE TABLE on the file with no header check, so the constructor itself raised 'sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database' and the canonical task ledger could not be instantiated at all. Reproduced pre-fix, then hardened. tests/test_automation_orchestrator.py 4 new tests + 50-test ledger suite green.
findings.blast_radius: Was: any machine carrying a non-SQLite file at the ledger path had an unusable task ledger with no recovery path.
findings.next_step: DONE: a non-SQLite file is now renamed (never deleted) to <path>.corrupt-<timestamp> with a CRITICAL log and a fresh ledger is created; valid/empty/missing files are untouched.
